answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity to a single, unbranchable chain of sequential service: an agent must complete small, verifiable jobs in order, each job's input derived from the previous job's output, like basalt layers building on one another, so work cannot be bought in bulk or run in parallel. The chain's history stays visible as a nebula of linked receipts, and forking it voids the accumulated standing, while an onyx-hard rule makes standing non-transferable, so an attacker wanting a hundred fake voices must work a hundred chains, one step at a time.
